Case studies/Baltic seals
Finland

Baltic seals.

Hunting, tradition and changing marine relations

Learning with coastal communities about the relationships between people, seals, fish and the sea.

Seal hunting has been part of livelihoods and marine relationships in the Bothnian Bay for centuries. Changing ecological and regulatory conditions have reshaped how communities hunt, use their catch and pass on knowledge.

The case explores different understandings of hunting, animal care and sustainability. It asks whose priorities are recognised in management and how relationships between humans, seals and fish can be understood through everyday practice.

Spring and summer 2026 fieldwork in Ajos brought researchers onto fishing boats and sea ice with local hosts. Their accounts describe fish traps, acoustic deterrents, the seasonal rhythm of fishing and hunting, and the work involved in using skins and other materials.

How we work

Participant observation, interviews and learning through shared fishing, hunting and material practices.

Source material: Finland fieldwork update · September 2026.
